Title: Three remanded over RM51,000 false claims for wedding catering
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has remanded three individuals, including a former manager of a frozen food company, for allegedly submitting false claims amounting to RM51,000.
Senior Assistant Registrar Yuhanis Mohd Roslan issued the remand order following an application by the MACC at the Kuala Terengganu magistrate's court today.
The male suspect was remanded for four days until July 30, while the two female suspects were remanded for three days until July 29.
Sources said the suspects, aged in their 20s and 30s, were arrested at 2pm yesterday after giving their statements at the state MACC headquarters.
"Initial investigations revealed the three suspects are believed to have colluded in committing the offence between May and June 2023.
"They are suspected of submitting false claims for wedding food package supplies involving three payment transfers into a company bank account and two personal bank accounts belonging to the suspects," the source said.
Terengganu MACC director Hazrul Shazreen Yazid confirmed the arrests, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fuziah: Competition Act amendments aim to curb cartels, monopolies driving up living costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Amendments to the Competition Act 2010 (Act 712) aim to curb cartels, monopolies, and anti-competitive practices driving up the cost of living.
Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the Competition (Amendment) Bill 2026 will strengthen the Malaysia Competition Commission's (MyCC) ability to counter tactics used by enterprises to evade enforcement.
She said the government must stop businesses taking shortcuts to maximise profits rather than competing fairly.
"These profits are not gained through healthy competition, but through anti-competitive practices such as price-fixing, market sharing, bid rigging in government procurement, and abuse of dominant or monopoly positions.
"Consequently, consumers and other businesses suffer through higher prices, limited product choices, and lower quality. This directly contributes to rising living costs," she said when tabling the bill for its second reading in the Dewan Negara today.
Fuziah said fair market competition encourages enterprises to boost efficiency, innovation, and product quality, allowing consumers to enjoy competitive prices.
She noted that a digital economy and new business models have made anti-competitive practices more complex and harder to detect.
"In enforcing Act 712, MyCC faces hurdles that hinder its efficiency. Today's market landscape has changed. Cartels and dominant players are increasingly creative in their modus operandi," she said.
She added that the amendments will bolster enforcement provisions, MyCC's investigative powers, decision-making procedures, and appeal mechanisms under the Competition Appeal Tribunal.
On July 6, the Dewan Rakyat passed the bill, comprising 34 clauses to strengthen Act 712.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SUV driver held after cops find RM6,000 in smuggled bromeliad plants
Article:
PASIR MAS: A 31-year-old motorist was arrested yesterday after General Operations Force personnel found 30 bromeliad plants worth more than RM6,000, believed to have been smuggled from Thailand, in his vehicle.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the seizure was made during Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan about 6.30pm.
He said GOF personnel from the Ninth Battalion were conducting motorcycle patrols in the Heram Perdah area when they spotted a Mitsubishi Pajero travelling along Jalan Bukit Lata towards Jeram Perdah.
"The team stopped the vehicle and checks uncovered 30 bromeliad plants in the rear compartment of the vehicle.
"The driver failed to produce the required documents, so the plants are believed to have been smuggled into the country through an illegal jetty along the border," he said.
Radzi said the driver, the vehicle and the plants were later seized.
"Early investigations revealed that the suspect was to deliver the plants to customers in Pasir Mas," he said.
The case has been referred to the Kelantan Agriculture Department for further investigation under Section 6 of the Plant Quarantine Act 1976.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's Prabowo approval rating drops to 51.1 per cent, survey finds
Article:
JAKARTA: The approval rating of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto fell to 51.1 per cent in July 2026, a poll showed, with respondents pointing to the state of the country's economy more than a year and a half into his term of office.
Prabowo's approval rating stood at 81.2 per cent in November 2025, before falling to 66.4 per cent in a survey conducted between late February and early March, Deni Irvani, executive director of Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting (SMRC), said during a livestreamed press conference on Sunday.
"Public perceptions of a deteriorating national economy were the main factor behind the decline in satisfaction with his performance," Irvani said.
Nearly half of the respondents, or 49.4 per cent, said economic conditions were either "bad" or "very bad", with just 15.7 per cent saying the economy was doing well, down from 40 per cent in November.
The survey confirmed the opinions of some economists that while Indonesia's economic growth figures are accurate, they do not reflect perceptions of prosperity on an individual level, Irvani said.
Dissatisfaction about the political situation as well as the state of law enforcement have also undermined Prabowo's popularity, he added.
The survey collected the opinions of 749 respondents from July 5 to 19, and has an estimated margin of error of 3.7 per cent.
As many as 42.8 per cent of the respondents said Prabowo's handling of the political situation was "bad" or "very bad", up sharply from 23 per cent in November.
The number who approved of his political performance has fallen to 13.5 per cent compared to 35.8 per cent in November.
On law enforcement, 37.6 per cent of the respondents said conditions were either "bad" or "very bad."
Prabowo took office in October 2024 after a sweeping general election victory on promises to stamp out corruption and increase economic opportunities by accelerating annual gross domestic product growth from five  to eight per cent.
However, his administration has been reeling this year under the impact of a depreciating currency and a poorly performing stock market, as well as concerns about overspending and the independence of the central bank.
One of the key parts of Prabowo's election campaign was an ambitious free-meals programme launched in January 2025, but the programme has been riddled with problems and its budget has been cut twice.
Despite the cuts, Indonesia's budget deficit is still expected to widen to 2.85 per cent of GDP this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Simpang Ampat shooting: Witness mistook gunshots for exploding lorry tyre
Article:
SIMPANG AMPAT: A witness initially mistook the sound of gunfire for a burst trailer lorry tyre before discovering a wounded man had run into her eatery seeking refuge.
The woman, who declined to be named, said she was at the cashier's counter with several employees when they heard a series of loud bangs about 10am.
She said they did not immediately suspect the sounds were gunshots as the shop is located along a busy road frequently used by lorries,
where tyre blowouts are not uncommon.
"We thought it was a truck or trailer lorry tyre bursting because heavy vehicles pass through here all the time.
"A short while later, a man suddenly ran into the shop. That was when we realised there had been a shooting outside," she said.
The woman said she did not witness the gunman opening fire because she and her employees immediately took cover after seeing a man enter the premises holding a pistol.
"As soon as we saw him with a gun, we all ducked and hid. We only got up after everything had quietened down and there were no more gunshots.
"Only then did we realise a man had been injured," she added.
She believed the victim was not one of her customers but had fled from a nearby shop before entering the eatery to seek shelter.
The woman said she was grateful the restaurant was not crowded at the time, as most breakfast customers had already left for work.
"Fortunately, there were not many customers. Had it happened earlier, the situation could have been far more chaotic," she said.
The
New Straits Times
earlier reported that a 38-year-old man
suffered a gunshot wound
to his right hand after a gunman allegedly fired at least five shots before fleeing in a car.
The 10am incident happened outside a row of shophouses in Jalan Perniagaan Seri Tambun here.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil prices dip over 6pct after US, Iran pause fighting over weekend
Article:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices tumbled more than six per cent on Monday after the US and Iran paused strikes over the weekend after two weeks of attacks, raising hopes of a diplomatic solution that would de-escalate the conflict and allow shipping to resume in the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent crude futures fell US$6.20, or 6.4 per cent, to US$90.58 by 0620 GMT after briefly slipping under the key support level of US$90 earlier in the session.
US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$83.51 a barrel, down US$5.80, or 6.5 per cent.
Both contracts are trading at their lowest levels in nearly a week after rising for the past three weeks.
Brent had reached US$100 per barrel as the conflict, which reduced oil shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, spilled over to the Red Sea, hindering exports from the world's top exporter, Saudi Arabia, via the Bab el-Mandeb strait to Asia.
The US ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, told "Fox News Sunday" and other US media that President Donald Trump had decided to pause US attacks to allow more time for diplomacy.
"Oil prices fell sharply in early trading as the US and Iran refrained from further military action, offering the first tangible signs of a potential de-escalation in tensions," said ING analysts in a client note.
"The price action in oil this morning clearly reflects the market's desperation for positive news."
Despite the pause in attacks, fewer than 10 commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz daily during the weekend, shipping data from Kpler showed.
"Any rebound in flows through the Strait of Hormuz is likely to prove slow and partial, as many shippers remain wary and will want greater confidence in their safety before they bring more empty ships into the Strait," MST Marquee analyst Saul Kavonic said.
In addition, ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb strait fell on Sunday after Yemeni Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast, although a third Chinese supertanker exited via the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
However, some analysts are still expecting markets to be supported if crude supplies stay affected by ongoing shipping risks in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war.
"As the Middle East conflict widened to the Red Sea and Ukrainian drones struck Russian ships and refineries ... Sustained (supply) disruption would likely keep oil prices elevated and continue to pose upside risks to global inflation," said UOB analysts in a note.
Ukraine said it hit several Russian oil sites over the weekend.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Body of Malaysian stabbed to death in South Korea to be repatriated
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The body of a Malaysian man who died after being
stabbed
during a group fight in South Korea will be repatriated after the necessary documentation is completed.
The family of 26-year-old Ahmad Shah is working with authorities in Eumseong County, North Chungcheong Province, to arrange the return of his remains.
His sister, Ain Sephia, 25, said her sister-in-law had confirmed that an autopsy on Ahmad's body had been completed.
She said the necessary documentation with the Malaysian Embassy in South Korea was still being finalised before the body could be released for repatriation.
"We have submitted all the required documents. Once the process is complete, arrangements will be made to bring the body home. There is no confirmed arrival date yet as several procedures remain," she said when contacted today.
Ahmad died after being stabbed during a group fight in South Korea. His family was informed about 2.40am after his wife, Nurcahaya Ruslan, called to inform them of his death.
South Korean media outlet JoongAng Daily reported that Eumseong police had arrested a Malaysian man in his 40s to assist in investigations.
The suspect is believed to have stabbed Ahmad with a knife during an altercation involving about 10 people at  3am along a street in Daeso-eup, Eumseong County.
Preliminary investigations found that two groups, including the suspect and victim, were involved in a large fight before the suspect allegedly pulled out a knife and attacked Ahmad.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea's ex-president found guilty of election disinformation
Article:
SEOUL: A South Korean court handed jailed ex-president Yoon Suk Yeol an 18-month suspended sentence on Monday for spreading disinformation in his 2022 election campaign before his martial law bid.
The Seoul Central District Court ruling could see South Korea's main opposition People Power Party (PPP), which Yoon represented, forced to pay 39.7 billion won (US$29 million) to the election commission if it is upheld on appeal.
It could also see Yoon's 2022 electoral win nullified, a largely symbolic blow for the disgraced ex-leader who is already serving a life sentence for insurrection.
Yoon declared martial law in December 2024, ordering troops to shut parliament, before MPs rallied to vote it down after just six hours and oust him.
The 65-year-old and his close cohorts have since been prosecuted in a hail of criminal cases.
Monday's sentence, suspended for three years, was handed down by judges who found Yoon guilty of twin violations of polling legislation by making false statements on the 2022 election trail.
Yoon won the vote with a margin of just 0.7 per cent.
However, the court found he had been dishonest about his ties to a shaman and lied during an interview at a Buddhist conference to cover up a 2019 meeting with the mystic in a bid to skirt controversy.
Yoon wore a neutral expression as judges also ruled he had lied about introducing a lawyer to a tax official who was investigated for alleged bribery.
"The defendant, a leading candidate in the presidential election – a procedure for selecting the nation's highest public official – publicised false information regarding his specific actions to his advantage," said the ruling, read aloud on a livestream.
"There are sufficient grounds to determine that the voters' ability to make informed decisions – a value the offence of disseminating false information seeks to protect – was compromised by these incidents."
Yoon's legal team said in a statement to AFP there were "significant errors" in the judgment and said they would lodge an appeal.
Under South Korean law, the election commission reimburses parties for all their campaigning costs if they win more than 15 per cent of the vote – legislation designed to limit the influence of money in politics.
Candidates sentenced to prison for election offences – including airing false information – are mandated to be removed from office, with their campaign funds returned to the National Election Commission.
The PPP spent 39.7 billion won contesting 2022's presidential election, a spokeswoman told AFP, and expects to be forced to pay back the cash if the ruling is upheld.
That amount would total roughly one-third of the beleaguered party's assets, according to election commission filings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang agri exhibition posts RM2.3 million sales from over 200,000 visitors
Article:
KUANTAN: The rebranded Pahang Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) in Raub concluded on a high note yesterday, recording RM2.3 million in sales and surpassing its RM1.3 million target.
State Agriculture, Agro-based Industry, Biotechnology and Education Committee chairman Datuk Seri Ir Mohd Soffi Abd Razak said the four-day event attracted 212,374 visitors, more than double its initial target of 100,000, and featured more than 200 entrepreneurs.
"MAHA Pahang has achieved a proud and outstanding feat. A total of 212,374 visitors attended the event, which recorded RM2.3 million in sales and attracted more than 200 entrepreneurs.
"This achievement proves that the agriculture and agri-food sector continues to garner a positive response, and holds significant potential for development as a key driver of the state's economy," he said in a Facebook post today.
Soffi also expressed his appreciation to all parties, including government agencies, participants, entrepreneurs, farmers and livestock breeders, for their efforts in making this year's event a success.
Pahang introduced the mini-MAHA in 2025, a scaled-down version of the country's premier agricultural exposition held biennially at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park in Selangor.
The event was
rebranded
as MAHA Pahang this year.
On July 25, Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail announced that Lipis would host MAHA Pahang next year, with an allocation of RM3 million, up from RM2 million previously.
He said the third edition in Lipis would be held on a larger scale to further strengthen the development of the state's agricultural and entrepreneurship sectors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man shot after buying eggs in Simpang Ampat
Article:
SIMPANG AMPAT: A 38-year-old man with a previous criminal record was injured after he was shot outside a row of shophouses in Jalan Perniagaan Seri Tambun here today.
The shooting occurred at about 10am after the man, who had reportedly finished exercising at a nearby gym, stopped at a convenience store in the same building to buy eggs.
As he was about to enter his car, he was approached by a masked man wearing a black jacket, who fired several shots at him.
The victim ran into a nearby eatery, but the suspect pursued him and fired several more shots, with one shot hitting the victim's right hand.The suspect fled in a car.
The injured man was rushed to Seberang Jaya Hospital for treatment.
Seberang Prai Selatan district police chief Superintendent Jay January Siowou confirmed the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: School bullying: NUTP backs appointing military veterans as full-time school wardens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP) supports appointing military veterans as full-time school wardens, with an initial rollout at selected fully residential schools.
Its president, Aminuddin Awang, said the Education Ministry's biggest challenge was managing nearly 1,900 boarding schools nationwide.
In contrast, Mara Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) have only 58 hostels, allowing for faster and more comprehensive implementation.
"That (recruiting military veterans as wardens) is a good proposal and can be implemented at selected fully residential schools as a starting point.
"At the same time, it must be noted that Mara only has 58 hostels compared with the Education Ministry, which has nearly 1,900. The effectiveness of hostel management cannot be directly compared," he said when contacted today.
He was commenting on Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki's proposal for the ministry to consider appointing full-time wardens from among military veterans to curb student bullying.
Aminuddin said NUTP had for years advocated appointing dedicated full-time wardens at all boarding schools.
"For NUTP, it does not matter whether they are veterans or non-veterans. What matters is having full-time wardens at boarding schools, especially fully residential schools.
"Creating full-time warden positions outside the teaching force is a realistic step towards curbing bullying and disciplinary misconduct while fostering student discipline," he said.
In February, the ministry reported 2,889 bullying cases last year, comprising 740 in primary schools and 2,149 in secondary schools.
Its Student Discipline System (SSDM) statistics showed a worrying upward trend, with bullying cases rising from 3,883 in 2022 to 6,528 in 2023 and 7,681 in 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Contractor loses RM122,552 in fake polytechnic tender scam
Article:
KUANTAN: A contractor lost RM122,552 after being tricked into making compulsory upfront payments for a non-existent polytechnic supply tender.
The 46-year-old victim only realised he had been duped after visiting the polytechnic last week to verify the status of the offer.
Kuantan police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the victim was contacted earlier this month by an individual claiming to be a polytechnic staff member, inviting his company to submit a quotation to supply a generator.
"The suspect produced an offer letter and introduced a supplier company.
"The victim made several payments totalling RM122,552 to a bank account provided by the suspect. The payments were purportedly for the purchase of goods required to fulfil the tender," he said in a statement today.
Ashari said the victim visited the polytechnic on July 23, where he was informed that no such tender had been issued.
The victim subsequently lodged a police report after he was unable to contact the suspect.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a jail sentence of between one and 10 years, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
On July 23, a 49-year-old
construction firm manager
also lost RM377,000 after falling victim to a fake tender offer involving the supply of electrical circuit boards.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nga: Political leaders must unite Malaysians, not divide them
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All political leaders must uphold moderation, mutual respect and national unity, says DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming.
The housing and local government minister said responsible leadership should focus on bringing Malaysians together instead of exploiting differences for political gain.
He said Malaysia's strength lies in its diversity, with people of different races, religions and backgrounds living harmoniously for generations while contributing collectively to the nation's progress and prosperity.
"Good leaders build bridges and foster more in common, not differences.
"Leadership is about uniting people around shared aspirations, not dividing them along racial or religious lines," he said in a Facebook post.
Nga said any attempt to manipulate racial sentiments, spread fear or sow distrust among communities would be detrimental to national cohesion and undermine the spirit of unity that had long been the foundation of Malaysia's success.
He said Malaysians were now more concerned about issues affecting their daily lives, including affordable housing, economic opportunities, quality public services, infrastructure development and a better future for their children.
"People want solutions, not division. They want leaders who can deliver results, create opportunities and improve their quality of life.
"Politics based on hatred and racial provocation has no place in a progressive and forward-looking Malaysia," he said.
Nga also urged voters to exercise wisdom and reject those seeking political mileage by creating division or manipulating racial sentiments.
"Malaysia's future should not be determined by those who seek to divide us.
"It should be shaped by leaders who inspire hope, promote understanding and bring people of all races together," he stressed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan Palace warns parties against dragging royalty into polls campaign
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Palace has reminded political parties against dragging the royal institution into state election campaigns.
Comptroller of the Royal Household Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said the royal institution remains neutral and is neither affiliated with any political party nor involved in political activities.
"The royal institution serves as a unifying force for the people, safeguarding harmony, stability and the nation's well-being.
"It upholds the principle of neutrality and does not side with any political party.
"Therefore, any claims, statements, photographs, videos or other materials linking the Negri Sembilan Palace, the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan or any member of the royal family to any political party are untrue," he said in a statement today.
Azizi urged all candidates contesting the state election to avoid raising 3R issues involving race, religion and royalty, and to conduct their campaigns responsibly, ethically and in accordance with the law to preserve harmony in the state.
He also thanked all parties for helping to ensure the royal institution continued to be respected and protected from misinterpretation or exploitation for political interests.
"The public is advised not to spread or believe unverified information and to rely on the Negri Sembilan Palace's official channels for accurate information."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's E&E sector gains from global supply chain shift, says UOB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's electrical and electronics (E&E) sector has emerged as one of the main beneficiaries of the global supply chain restructuring triggered by the escalation of US tariffs in April 2025.
UOB Global Economics & Markets Research said the renewed decoupling between the United States and China has accelerated the diversion of Chinese exports to alternative markets, particularly across Asia.
In a macroeconomic note, the firm said Asean has been among the biggest winners from the supply chain realignment, with manufacturing-driven economies such as Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia recording the strongest gains.
"For Malaysia, the E&E sector remains the primary channel through which these opportunities are materialising.
"Rising exports, expanding participation in artificial intelligence-related supply chains, stronger re-export activity and growing Chinese investment inflows all underscore Malaysia's increasing strategic importance in regional manufacturing networks," it said.
UOB said the E&E industry has become an increasingly important export driver, accounting for 48.2 per cent of Malaysia's total exports in the first half of 2026, up from 44.2 per cent in 2025 and about 40 per cent in both 2023 and 2024.
The firm said trade diversion appears to be contributing significantly to growth in electronics exports.
"Notably, electronic integrated circuits (HS 8542) dominated re-export activity, with re-exports equivalent to 41.8 per cent of total HS 8542 exports.
"While this supports export growth, it also suggests that part of Malaysia's trade expansion reflects its role as a transit or intermediate processing hub rather than a source of fully domestic production."
UOB said another sign of this trend is the changing trade balance within the E&E sector.
Malaysia's E&E trade surplus narrowed between 2024 and 2025 as larger surpluses with the US were increasingly offset by widening deficits with upstream suppliers, particularly China and Taiwan.
"This points to Malaysia importing more intermediate goods from regional supply chain partners while exporting higher volumes to final markets, particularly the US," it said.
Investment trends also suggest Malaysia is becoming more deeply integrated into regional production networks.
Net foreign direct investment (FDI) from China and Hong Kong stood at RM13.3 billion in 2025, compared with RM18.3 billion in 2024.
Meanwhile, net FDI through Singapore more than doubled to RM53.4 billion in 2025.
"Over the years, Malaysia has attracted a diverse mix of FDI from Asia, the Americas and the European Union," the firm said.
UOB said Malaysia continues to be viewed as a relative safe haven amid heightened global uncertainty and the broader impact of the Middle East conflict on Asia, supported by stable economic fundamentals and a favourable growth outlook.
However, it cautioned that the growing emphasis on rules of origin and anti-transshipment measures means future gains will increasingly depend on stronger domestic value creation.
"Malaysia's long-term competitiveness will hinge on its ability to deepen local manufacturing capabilities, enhance technological sophistication and capture a larger share of value-added activities within the global electronics supply chain," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Felda's decline caused by political interference, says Anwar
Article:
TAMPIN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has attributed Felda's financial troubles to excessive political interference in its management.
He said the agency's decline was not caused by settlers but by those entrusted to lead it.
He said Felda, once regarded as the world's largest plantation organisation with annual profits running into billions of ringgit, had accumulated nearly RM10 billion in debt due to poor governance over the past several years.
"When I became prime minister, I was informed that Felda was carrying debts of almost RM10 billion.
"Previously, under the management of leaders such as the late Raja Alias (Tun Raja Muhammad Alias Raja Muhammad Ali) and (Tan Sri) Taib Andak, Felda was managed efficiently and became the largest plantation organisation in the world, generating billions of ringgit in profits annually.
"But seven or eight years ago, changes in management and excessive political interference resulted in an organisation that once made tens of billions in profits ending up with RM10 billion in losses," he said when addressing soldiers at Syed Sirajuddin Camp.
Anwar said the government was now allocating RM980 million annually to service Felda's losses.
"The settlers did not suddenly stop working hard. The problem lies with those entrusted with the responsibility and who betrayed that trust," he said.
Anwar said the episode underscored the importance of integrity among leaders entrusted with managing public institutions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sweden's far-right leader Akesson brought fringe party to brink of power
Article:
IT'S no coincidence that it sounded like the start of a rock concert when Swedish far-right leader Jimmie Akesson strode onto the stage to chants of "Jimmie! Jimmie! Jimmie!" from a crowd of supporters, some wearing his face on their T-shirts.
Akesson, who is now 47 and has led the Sweden Democrats since he was 25, plays keyboards in a Viking rock band and had a heavy metal-themed wedding two years ago, with guests singing karaoke and no dress code.
His rowdy live act at political rallies is part of the appeal of a party that has become Sweden's second largest.
Now, after decades being shunned by the mainstream, and four years propping up a centre-right minority government from the sidelines, he aims to win a share of political power for the first time in an election in September.
The party, which acknowledges that some of its founders were neo-Nazis, says that it now has a strict "no racism" policy.
But a poll last year found that half of Swedish voters still view the Sweden Democrats as racist, and opponents say they can still plainly hear open bigotry in some of Akesson's remarks.
"It's our politics that ensures that those who make an effort, go to work, will have a better, safer and freer life than the neighbouring couple who sit at home with their eight children and watch Arabic soap operas," Akesson told the rally to loud applause.
In an interview with Reuters, Akesson said patience had been key to the party's success as he built support from around two per cent of the electorate to its present levels, 10 times as big.
"I said already in my inauguration speech as party leader in 2005 that we will become a large party with great influence over politics, that we will eventually be a government party and challenge the Social Democrats as the largest party," he said.
Akesson, usually dressed in a suit but with no tie, cultivates a relaxed persona.
[[nid:1498059]]
Despite being the longest-serving party leader in parliament, he still lives in his hometown in southern Sweden and commutes weekly to attend the Riksdag in Stockholm.
"He's not up on a high horse and he has a knack for explaining complicated issues in an easy, understandable way," said Jenny Madestam, a political scientist at Sodertorn University. "He is the guy next door."
The Sweden Democrats were founded in 1988 as a radical nationalist party.
According to an internal investigation, some founders were neo-Nazis, including a Swede who fought in the German SS during World War Two.
Early party material shows antisemitism and racism were common.
Akesson joined the party in 1995, shortly after it began distancing itself from its most radical ideologies.
It expelled extremist members, banned uniforms at official gatherings and urged members to abandon steel-toed boots and bomber jackets.
Akesson said it was the party's opposition to the European Union that convinced him to join, though he dropped the policy of seeking "Swexit" in 2019.
After taking over as party leader in 2005, Akesson embarked on a strategy to broaden the party's appeal and build a more conventional political organisation.
Together with a close-knit group of allies known as the "Gang of Four", he established local party organisations to contest municipal elections.
"It was a travelling circus," he said. "We went town to town and did everything from printing membership cards to talking policy. It was a really fun time, because we were making such progress."
Scandals have continued to surface. Last year one of the party's lawmakers had to step down after he was caught owning a vast collection of Nazi memorabilia, including two early editions of Mein Kampf and fan pictures of Hitler.
But the party insists it has left extremism behind.
"There were severe problems in the party's earliest childhood," said Mattias Karlsson, member of parliament for the Sweden Democrats and author of the party's ideological programme.
"But today, I don't think it is worse than in other parties."
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Malaysia needs only RM16mil for Sepang F1 preparations, says Anwar
Article:
TAMPIN: Malaysia will only need to spend an estimated RM16 million to prepare the Sepang International Circuit for the return of Formula One, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said Bahrain had agreed to absorb the substantial upfront payment to the International Automobile Federation (FIA) after deciding to relocate its Grand Prix to Malaysia due to regional security concerns.
He said the arrangement meant Malaysia would only need to carry out minor maintenance works on the Sepang circuit.
"The initial payment of hundreds of millions of ringgit had already been paid to Formula One by Bahrain. We do not have to pay it.
"We are effectively hosting it for free. If there is any expenditure, it is only to carry out minor repairs to the track, which is currently used for other racing events.
"I expect that to cost between RM10 million and RM16 million," he said when attending the Semarak Kenegaraan programme with members of the armed forces today at Syed Sirajuddin Camp.
Anwar said the amount was significantly lower than the costs typically incurred by countries hosting Formula One races.
"Other countries spend hundreds of millions, even up to RM1 billion, to organise Formula One. We have only been asked to spend RM16 million, yet Malaysia will become the focus of the world.
"All the world's top drivers, the most advanced racing cars and thousands of engineers will be coming to Sepang," he said.
He said the opportunity reflected international confidence in Malaysia's stability, infrastructure and ability to organise major global events efficiently.
Anwar added that the government's priority would be ensuring a safe and secure environment throughout the event, with the armed forces, police, Immigration Department and Customs Department playing key roles in maintaining security and facilitating the smooth arrival of teams and spectators.
Yesterday, Formula 1 and the governing body FIA had announced that Sepang would host the Bahrain Grand Prix as a replacement race on the 2026 calendar.
The race, subject to final agreements and approval by the World Motor Sport Council, will be held between the Azerbaijan and Singapore rounds.
The event will mark Formula 1's return to Sepang, which last hosted a championship race in 2017.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Royal diplomacy brings Bahrain F1 Grand Prix to Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Royal diplomacy between His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain's King Hamad Isa Al Khalifa has paved the way for the return of Formula One (F1) to Malaysia after an eight-year absence.
The Bahrain Grand Prix will be staged at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit following discussions between the two monarchs, according to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page today.
The agreement came after the Bahrain Grand Prix faced uncertainty due to armed conflict in the Middle East, which disrupted the F1 calendar and threatened the race.
King Hamad had contacted Sultan Ibrahim by phone to discuss a solution, leading to strategic cooperation between the Malaysian and Bahraini governments, Formula One, and the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), said the post.
"In efforts to find a solution, the King of Bahrain held discussions with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong through a phone call.
"The understanding led to an agreement to stage the Bahrain Formula 1 Grand Prix at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit, bringing Formula 1 back to Malaysia after it was last held in 2017," it said.
The Palace said the development reflected the "close friendship and high level of trust" between Sultan Ibrahim and King Hamad, whose personal ties began in 2017 and were further strengthened during Sultan Ibrahim's state visit to Bahrain in 2025.
It added that the announcement had been well received by F1 fans in Malaysia and across the region, describing it as "a historic chapter" that reflected the strong diplomatic ties between the two monarchs.
Formula 1 and the FIA confirmed yesterday that Sepang would host the
Bahrain Grand Prix
from Oct 2 to 4, after plans to reschedule the race in Bahrain later this year were derailed by escalating conflict in the region.
The race will be held between the Azerbaijan and Singapore rounds of the championship.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Any action taken based on Tabung Haji RCI must follow due process
Article:
TAMPIN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said whether the cabinet decides to publicly release the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Tabung Haji, whatever legal action is taken must follow due process.
The prime minister said any action taken based on the RCI must also be free of political interference.
"In our system, investigations are conducted by the investigating authorities, charges are brought by the attorney-general, and judgments are made by the judges.
"As prime minister, my responsibility is to ensure the process remains free (of political interference) and follows the Federal Constitution and the laws that have been established," he said.
Anwar was speaking when attending the Semarak Kenegaraan programme with members of the armed forces today at Syed Sirajuddin Camp here.
Anwar reietrated that he hopes the cabinet will decide on Wednesday to make the report public.
"We do not want to comment at length on the issue. Hopefully, at the cabinet meeting on Wednesday, we will make a decision.
"There is a report. Let the people read it. If someone has done nothing wrong, defend them. If they have committed an offence, they should be charged.
"If they are convicted and sent to prison, then they should go to prison. That is not my decision,"
Yesterday, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi expressed support for Anwar's intention to make the report public.
Zahid said he hoped the report would be removed from the list under the Official Secrets Act (OSA).
Anwar said, as prime minister, he must remain honest in carrying out his duties and ensure that every process must adhere to the Federal Constitution and established regulations.
"I raise this issue (the TH RCI) because, to me, the nation cannot safeguard its peace if those entrusted with responsibility betray that trust," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Remand extended for two men in murder of 10-year-old girl
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The remand order for two men detained over the murder of a 10-year-old girl, whose body was found in Sepanggar last week, has been extended until Friday (July 31).
Investigating officer Assistant Superintendent La Paula Abd Muis said the extension was granted for another week to allow police to complete investigations.
The two suspects — a 39-year-old undocumented man and a 42-year-old local man — were initially remanded for seven days until July 24 before police applied for an extension.
They were
arrested
following the discovery of Nurjilya Abdullah whose body was found on an overgrown slope near a house under construction in Kampung Numbak on July 16.
It was reported that the post-mortem examination found that Nurjilya died from injuries to her face and the back of her head, believed to have been caused by a hard, blunt object.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FWCMS helps curb foreign workers abuse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Foreign Worker Centralised Management System (FWCMS), developed by Bestinet Sdn Bhd, has helped curb the exploitation of foreign workers by cartels and prevent such practices from becoming more widespread in Malaysia.
Senior lecturer in economics at the Department of Economics and Financial Studies of Universiti Teknologi Mara Selangor branch Dr Nurul Ainun Ahmad Atory said foreign worker cartels could have become more entrenched without FWCMS.
The system replaced fragmented manual counter processes with a single digital platform, she added.
Nurul Ainun said the previous manual system created opportunities for exploitation and abuse, whereas a centralised digital platform has helped improve governance and transparency.
"A centralised digital system has the potential to reduce transaction costs, speed up application processing and enhance transparency through systematic digital records and audit trails.
"From an institutional economics perspective, such a mechanism can reduce information asymmetry.
"This helps narrow opportunities for rent-seeking activities, abuse of power and the involvement of intermediaries that do not add value to the economy," she said.
Her remarks came in response to a recent news report highlighting how foreign worker cartels have continued to operate with apparent impunity, with the masterminds behind these syndicates allegedly reaping millions of ringgits in profits while evolving their modus operandi to evade enforcement.
Earlier, Micro Traders Association of Malaysia (MAMBA) chairman Tan Peng Beng cautioned that politicising FWCMS could undermine the meaningful progress achieved in strengthening governance, efficiency and transparency in Malaysia's foreign worker recruitment management.
He said the absence of the system would risk reversing the improvements made in enhancing governance and streamlining the country's foreign worker management process.
Commenting further, Nurul Ainun said the effectiveness of any digital system should not be assessed solely on its existence, but must instead be supported by empirical evidence and sustained enforcement.
She said the system should be evaluated based on clear indicators, including lower foreign worker recruitment costs, shorter processing times and improved employer compliance.
"This should also include a reduction in fraud cases and an increase in government revenue.
"If these objectives are achieved consistently, systems such as FWCMS will not only improve economic efficiency but also strengthen investor confidence in Malaysia's business ecosystem through more transparent, efficient and accountable governance," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SevenCo launches RM192mil Penang affordable housing project as demand stays firm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SevenCo Prestige Sdn Bhd has launched Sevora Residence, a RM192 million freehold affordable housing development in Bukit Mertajam, Penang, as demand for value-driven homes continues to underpin the state's residential market.
The project comprises 420 Rumah Mampu Milik (RMM) PN1 units priced between RM388,000 and RM489,200, targeting first-time homebuyers, young families and owner-occupiers seeking quality homes in Seberang Perai, one of Penang's fastest-growing residential and industrial corridors.
Located on a 1.398-hectare site along Jalan Song Ban Kheng, the project comprises a 34-storey residential tower with 420 units and eight commercial lots.
The development comes as Penang's property market continues to benefit from steady demand, supported by ongoing industrial expansion, infrastructure upgrades and employment growth, particularly in Seberang Perai, where improved connectivity and the presence of manufacturing and logistics hubs have boosted housing demand.
Each residential unit has a built-up area of 950 square feet (sq ft), featuring three bedrooms and two bathrooms, while the commercial lots range from 1,077 sq ft to 1,987 sq ft.
SevenCo chairman Jeffery Chung said home ownership is one of the biggest financial commitments people make, making it essential for developments to deliver lasting value.
"At SevenCo, we believe that price is what buyers pay today, but true value is what homeowners continue to enjoy every day after they move in," he said.
Chung said the company focuses on creating practical and comfortable living spaces that enhance residents' quality of life rather than simply building homes.
The project incorporates features such as beamless living rooms, separate dry and wet bathroom areas, fitted kitchen cabinets and layouts designed to provide greater privacy.
Residents will also have access to facilities including a swimming pool, children's lagoon, sky lounge, gymnasium, multipurpose hall, yoga deck, wellness garden, barbecue area, jogging path and recreational parks.
Other amenities include wider corridors, dual drop-off areas, visitor parking with electric vehicle charging readiness and unit layouts positioned to minimise noise from lift areas.
The project is scheduled for completion in the second quarter of 2030.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia to suspend trading in BHIC Securities on Aug 7
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia will suspend trading in the securities of Boustead Heavy Industries Corporation Bhd (BHIC) from 9am on Friday, Aug 7, 2026, to facilitate the implementation of the company's selective capital reduction and repayment exercise.
Bursa Malaysia said that the exercise would be undertaken pursuant to Section 116 of the Companies Act 2016.
Bursa Malaysia also advised investors to refer to BHIC's announcement dated July 24, 2026, as well as the notice to shareholders and redeemable convertible preference shareholders dated July 27, 2026, for further details.
At 12.30pm, BHIC shares rose one sen to 48 sen, with 37,600 shares traded.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM5bil financing pool to back Malaysian startups over 18 months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than RM5 billion in financing will be channelled through 15 funding agencies and financial institutions over the next 18 months, as Putrajaya steps up efforts to help Malaysian technologies reach the market.
Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said the funding pool will support startups and innovators at different stages of growth, although applicants must meet the eligibility criteria set by each participating institution.
"We have connected 15 organisations, including funding agencies and financial institutions. Together, they provide funding worth about RM5 billion to support our startups and innovators," he told reporters after launching the TechnoMART Malaysia: High Tech Financing 2026 event at MBSB Bank Tower today.
Among the participating organisations are the Malaysian Research Accelerator for Technology and Innovation, MBSB Bank and EXIM Bank Malaysia.
Asked whether the RM5 billion was allocated for this year alone, Chang said it is an aggregated funding pool from the participating organisations covering about one-and-a-half years.
He stressed that the financing is not distributed automatically but is subject to the respective institutions' eligibility requirements.
In his speech, Chang said Malaysia has no shortage of talent, creativity or breakthrough technologies, with universities, research institutions, startups and industries producing innovations in areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors, biotechnology, advanced manufacturing and green technology.
However, he said many promising technologies fail to reach the market because they struggle to secure financing, partnerships and market access during the commercialisation stage, commonly known as the "valley of death".
"Too many promising technologies fail not because they lack potential, but because they lack access to the right financing, partnerships and market opportunities at the right time," he said.
Chang said Malaysia's innovation ecosystem has continued to strengthen, citing the country's ranking of 34th out of 139 economies in the Global Innovation Index 2025 and its rise by eight places to 15th out of 70 countries in the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking 2026.
He said the country's success should ultimately be measured by the number of globally competitive technology companies it produces, the creation of high-value jobs, the commercialisation of Malaysian intellectual property, and the impact of innovation on people's lives.
He said Malaysia must become a creator and exporter of strategic technologies, rather than merely a consumer, particularly in fields such as AI, quantum technologies, semiconductors, biotechnology and clean energy.
Chang said innovation-led growth requires collaboration between the government, industry and financial institutions, as technology companies require different forms of financing throughout their development journey, ranging from grants and equity financing to debt, guarantees, blended finance and working capital.
He said TechnoMART Malaysia aims to bridge the gap between innovators and investors by bringing technology developers, financiers, industry players and government agencies together under one platform.
Beyond financing, participating companies will also gain access to technical assessments, business advisory services, strategic partnerships, certification support and market access to accelerate commercialisation and growth.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka Customs seizes RM8.36mil shark fins declared as fish skin
Article:
MELAKA: The Customs Department has foiled an attempt to smuggle 5,069kg of shark fins worth RM8.36 million after an importing company declared the cargo as fish skin.
Melaka Customs director Roslan Yusoff said the shark fins, believed to have been imported from Guyana, South America, were seized on July 2.
He said the smuggling attempt was allegedly masterminded by a company based in Selangor, with efforts underway to locate its director to assist in investigations.
The seizure followed an inspection by the Melaka Customs Enforcement Division and Narcotics Branch from headquarters of a container at Port Klang, Selangor.
"Checks revealed that the cargo was declared as fish skin under a tariff code subject to a five per cent tax.
"However, physical inspection found 180 gunny sacks containing 5,069kg of shark fins, which should have been declared under a different tariff code with a 10 per cent tax rate and required inspection and approval from the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (Maqis) and Fisheries Department under CITES provisions," he said.
Roslan said this at a press conference at the Melaka Customs Building in Ayer Keroh today.
He said the shark fins were estimated to be worth RM7.6 million, while the total seizure, including duties and taxes, was valued at RM8.36 million.
A man in his 50s representing the shipping agent responsible for managing trade declaration documents was detained to assist in investigations before being released on bail.
The importing company is believed to have been operating for about five years, importing various goods, including seafood.
"We found that the syndicate's modus operandi was to make false declarations to avoid Maqis inspections and reduce tax payments.
"Investigations are also being conducted into the supplier from Guyana and the ordering parties to identify the entire network behind this operation," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 135(1)(a) of the Customs Act 1967 for importing uncustomed or prohibited goods.
Upon conviction, offenders face a fine of between 10 and 20 times the value of the goods or RM50,000 and RM500,000 respectively, whichever is higher, imprisonment for up to five years, or both.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Network School yet to appeal licence revocation, says Johor exco
Article:
KULAI: The Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) has yet to receive an appeal from Network School following the revocation of its business licence last week.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said no appeal application had been submitted to the local authority so far.
"It is cancelled completely. Simply put, they are illegal. If they form another company and meet the set conditions, it can be considered, but there has been no appeal so far," he said.
He said this at a press conference after officiating the TVET (Technical and Vocational Education and Training) and Kulai Municipal Career Carnival 2026 at Dewan Raya Putra in Bandar Putra today.
Jafni said MBIP took action after identifying two clear licensing violations committed by the company.
"At the MBIP level, as everyone knows, there were two clear infractions. First, the advertisement signage failed to comply with conditions, so we cancelled it.
"At the same time, the licence applied for differed significantly from their actual operations, which breached the licensing terms," he said.
However, he said the state government continues to welcome new investments and gave assurance that Johor remains an investor-friendly state.
The Bukit Permai assemblyman added that any action against the company owners falls under the jurisdiction of the Johor State Legal Adviser.
Last Wednesday, MBIP shut down and sealed
Network School's
premises in Forest City, Iskandar Puteri.
A day earlier, MBIP announced the cancellation of NSO Malaysia Sdn Bhd's (Network School) business licence and ordered all activities to cease effective July 22 due to licensing breaches.
The Johor government said in a statement that the enforcement action followed an MBIP Special Full Council Meeting decision, which confirmed the company had failed to adhere to the terms of its business licence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Far-right Australian politician loses appeal in racism case
Article:
SYDNEY: A popular far-right Australian politician failed on Monday to overturn a racial vilification finding that was handed down after she told a Muslim senator to go back to Pakistan.
Senator Pauline Hanson has emerged as one of Australia's most popular politicians, wooing voters with calls for strict immigration curbs, mass deportations of "illegal migrants" and enhanced free speech protections.
Hanson took aim at Pakistan-born Australian lawmaker Mehreen Faruqi in 2022 over comments made in the wake of Queen Elizabeth II's death.
Faruqi, a left-leaning Greens senator, said she could not mourn the "leader of a racist empire built on stolen lives, land and wealth of colonised people."
Hanson replied on social media: "When you immigrated to Australia you took every advantage of this country.
"You took citizenship, bought multiple homes, and a job in a parliament.
"It's clear you're not happy, so pack your bags and piss off back to Pakistan."
The Federal Court of Australia found in 2024, in response to a complaint from Faruqi, that Hanson's comments amounted to a "strong form of racism."
Hanson's appeal against that decision on free speech grounds was dismissed on Monday.
"I was incensed by the incredible disrespect that I felt was shown to our late Queen on the day of her death by Senator Faruqi and others," she said after the court's decision.
"I simply wanted to call that out."
For years a political outsider, Hanson's One Nation has surged this year to become one of the country's most popular parties, according to opinion polls.
Hanson has pledged sweeping cuts to government spending – akin to Elon Musk's "DOGE" in the United States – and has urged Australia to rethink its membership of international organisations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Seattle shooting suspect in custody, local media reports 2 dead, 5 injured
Article:
SEATTLE: At least two people were killed and five others, including a 2-year-old child, were wounded on Sunday in a shooting at a downtown Seattle food festival, local news outlets reported, with the US city's mayor's office saying a suspect had been taken into custody.
Police urged people to avoid the area at the base of the famed Space Needle on Sunday evening as officers investigated the shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival.
"Multiple shooting victims. Shots fired at the Seattle Center," the department said on X. The Seattle Times and local TV station KOMO, citing the Seattle Fire Department, reported the death and injury toll.
Witnesses told the Times they heard several shots around 6 pm local time (0100 GMT).
"What happened at the Seattle Center today was an act of horrific violence," Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said in a statement, adding a suspect had been taken into custody.
"Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives, and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin: No let-up in Immigration action despite over-capacity depots
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Home Ministry will not reduce the momentum of Immigration Department enforcement operations against foreigners who violate the Immigration Act.
This is despite all 19 detention depots nationwide currently operating beyond capacity, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said enforcement must continue as it involves matters of national security and sovereignty, in addition to ensuring foreigners in Malaysia comply with the law.
"Our country is open, they can come here to earn a living, but our country also has laws with which they must comply.
"Don't enter without documents, don't overstay, don't misuse your pass... if we find such cases, we have the power to bring them to the depot.
"(Immigration Deputy director-general of operations Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli) cannot reduce the momentum of these raids at all, because this is a matter of security and also a matter of sovereignty," he said in his speech at the Home Ministry's monthly assembly here today.
Saifuddin said the issue of overcrowded depots often draws criticism from various parties, including non-governmental organisations that raise humanitarian concerns, but the government has to balance law enforcement with the welfare of detainees.
He said the more enforcement is intensified, the more cases are uncovered.
Sharing details of a bilateral meeting, Saifuddin said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto had expressed appreciation to Malaysia for giving his countrymen the opportunity to earn a living here, while stressing that action should still be taken against them under the law if they commit offences.
"He (Prabowo) stressed that if Indonesian citizens violate Malaysia's domestic laws, then the Malaysian government needs to take action according to the laws of this country," he said.
More than
22,000 undocumented migrants
are currently being held at immigration depots nationwide, with some detainees having been held for years, including one who has been detained for 11 years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anthony Loke slams ‘baseless’ Adat interference claims, says rivals scapegoating DAP amid royal crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 27 — DAP secretary general Anthony Loke has denied claims that he interfered in Negeri Sembilan’s Adat Perpatih institution, describing the allegations as baseless.
According to
Malaysiakini
, the Chennah assemblyman said rumours linking him to the ongoing royal dispute in the state were unfounded, including suggestions that he had channelled funds to a faction opposed to Sungai Ujong chieftain Mubarak Thahak.
“These are completely baseless and illogical claims. Yet, some people believe them,” he told voters in Kampung Sungai Rotan.
“We respect the Yang di Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, the four Undangs, and the Tunku Besar of Tampin.”
Loke stressed that matters relating to Adat Perpatih were handled within the traditional system itself and insisted there was no reason for him to interfere. He added that he and his party were being made scapegoats by political rivals,
Malaysiakini
reported.
The allegations surfaced amid a wider dispute in Negeri Sembilan, where Barisan Nasional (BN) has accused the Pakatan Harapan state government of mishandling the situation, prompting the four chieftains to invoke their authority to remove ruler Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Rumours also claimed that Loke had channelled substantial funds to nobles opposed to Mubarak. His political secretary has since lodged a police report against former Bersatu leader Badrul Hisham Shaharin, better known as Chegubard, over a social media post making the allegation.
Loke said the crisis was triggered when 14 Umno assemblymen led by Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Jalaluddin Alias withdrew their support for the Harapan led state government.
He argued that the state administration had been stable for three years until the withdrawal, which he suggested was motivated by political ambition.

Title: Fire breaks out at hilly forest area in Bandar Puncak Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, July 27 —  A fire involving an estimated two-acre hilly forest area in Bandar Puncak Alam broke out this morning, with firefighting operations currently underway.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 10.06 am,  prompting the deployment of a team from the Bestari Jaya Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) to the scene.
“Fire engines arrived at the location at 10.34 am and found that the fire involved a hilly forest area estimated to be about two acres in size.
“Firefighters are currently constructing firebreaks and carrying out extinguishing operations with assistance from the Saujana Volunteer Firefighting Team (PBS),” he said in a statement today.
Ashrul Riezal said the operation involves four personnel and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) from BBP Bestari Jaya, while PBS Saujana deployed four members to assist in controlling the blaze.
No casualties have been reported so far, and firefighting efforts are ongoing. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says govt reviewing promotion process for senior military officers
Article:
TAMPIN, July 27 — The government is reviewing the promotion process for senior officers of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) to ensure their career progression is not unduly delayed, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the matter warrants attention as promotions for senior military officers can sometimes take longer than those for other public sector employees.
Anwar noted that civil servants, including members of the security forces, had already benefited from the revised salary structure under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA).
“Among senior officers (of the MAF), promotions can sometimes take longer compared with other civil servants. I have asked the Chief Secretary to the Government (Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar) whether we can review the process.
“The number involved is not large, but we need to assess the financial implications. We will decide on this soon so that our armed forces know they are neither left behind nor marginalised. Insya-Allah, we’ll get on it,” he said at the Semarak Kenegaraan programme at Syed Sirajuddin Camp here today.
Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief of Defence Forces General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
Anwar said the proposal had already been discussed and would be finalised at a meeting that he would chair soon. — Bernama

Title: New Statistics Bill aims to modernise Malaysia’s data system, says Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The Statistics Bill 2026 is expected to be gazetted by the end of this year after completing the administrative process following its approval in Parliament, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said the bill had been approved in the Dewan Rakyat and was scheduled to be brought to the Dewan Negara next week, with the hope of gaining support before being enacted.
“We are targeting the end of this year... but it is an administrative process, meaning the stages that will be carried out, just like every time a bill is passed at the parliamentary level, the administrative process will follow,” he said at a press conference during the Ministry of Economy’s monthly assembly here today, when asked about the 2026 Statistics Bill.
He noted that after the bill is gazetted and comes into effect, the department will be known as the Department of Statistics Malaysia.
Akmal Nasrullah said the ministry would conduct a stakeholder engagement process after the bill is passed to enhance understanding of the importance of the new act.
He said the department would also hold engagement sessions with various parties to ensure the implementation of the act not only involves legal aspects but also brings about cultural changes to elevate the status of the country’s statistics.
Commenting on the independence of official statistics from political influence, he said the Statistics Bill 2026 strengthens governance through the establishment of the National Statistics Council, which will play a role in assessing the direction and development of the country’s statistics.
He said that the production of official statistics remains guided by the objective processes used by the Department of Statistics, including the periodic implementation of censuses such as the economic census and the agricultural census.
Akmal Nasrullah said the bill also emphasises the establishment of a data repository centre to coordinate data from various agencies, while ensuring the confidentiality of information.
“The ownership of the data does not mean it will be transferred to the Department of Statistics. But we are more focused on producing more comprehensive and detailed findings so that the data can be used as effectively as possible,” he emphasised.
Regarding access to data, he said researchers, journalists and stakeholders can submit a formal request to the chief statistician if the required information has not yet been published, subject to confidentiality requirements.
Akmal Nasrullah also said that the Statistics Bill 2026 provides a foundational framework to strengthen the use of data in the decision-making process, in addition to replacing the Statistics Act that has been in force for 61 years.
“This bill is intended to provide a framework that will serve as a foundation so that we have the space to move forward.
“Things that might have been limitations before are now more permissible because they no longer rely on the old traditional methods, but it’s also about how we modernise the way we understand statistics,” he added.
On July 16, the Dewan Rakyat approved the Statistics Bill 2026, which aims, among other things, to replace the Statistics Act 1965 (Act 415) to create a more modern, comprehensive legal framework that aligns with the current data and statistics ecosystem.
The bill was passed with a majority of votes after being debated by 21 Members of Parliament from both the government and opposition blocs. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar says Malaysia’s only cost for Bahrain F1 Grand Prix is RM16m Sepang track upgrades
Article:
TAMPIN, July 27 — Malaysia will not incur any registration fees from the International Automobile Federation (FIA) for hosting the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 at Sepang this October, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
“Alhamdulillah, after more than a decade we are hosting again. Back then, the costs ran into hundreds of millions when we staged it in 2017.
“This time, we are organising without paying registration fees to the company — it’s free,” he said in his speech at the Semarak Kenegaraan programme at Dewan Garisson, Kem Syed Sirajuddin in Gemas, as reported by
Berita Harian
(BH).
Formula 1 and the FIA yesterday confirmed that Malaysia will host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit, scheduled between the Azerbaijan and Singapore Grands Prix from October 2 to 4, 2026.
The event, which is subject to final agreements and official sign-off, including the approval of the World Motor Sport Council, will become the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the only expenditure Malaysia would bear is for upgrading the Sepang track, BH reported.
“About RM16 million is required annually to maintain the Sepang International Circuit in order to meet the standards set for hosting motorsport events.”
“Elsewhere, hosting costs run into hundreds of millions or at least RM1 billion. Here, we are asked to spend RM16 million — yet it will draw the world’s top drivers, the most advanced cars, and thousands of engineers flying into Sepang, Malaysia,” he was quoted as saying.
Anwar added that Malaysia was chosen to host the race over many other countries for three reasons.
“They looked at dozens of countries, if not more. First, it must be peaceful. Second, the administration must be efficient. Third, the infrastructure must be superior,” he said.

Title: IPCC receives 1,635 complaints against police since 2023, says Saifuddin
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, July 27 — The Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) has received 1,635 public complaints since it began operations in 2023 up to July 24, 2026, reflecting growing public confidence in its role as an independent police oversight body.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that of the total, 844 complaints, or 76 per cent, have been resolved, while 372 complaints were received this year as of July 24.
“The highest number of complaints involves complainants not receiving any feedback on reports they lodged against the police.
“But it is important to understand how the IPCC functions. It receives all complaints, but they are categorised accordingly. If a complaint contains elements of corruption, the IPCC will refer it to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC),” he said at a press conference after attending the Home Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the remaining unresolved complaints include cases involving complainants who were dissatisfied with the outcome of police investigations or had not received any response after lodging their complaints with the police.
He said a total of 22 investigation papers have been opened so far, including five this year, with 11 cases completed and the remaining 11 still under investigation.
Saifuddin Nasution said that although the number of complaints received since 2023 was relatively modest, it nevertheless reflected public confidence in the IPCC as a channel for lodging complaints against police misconduct.
Earlier, he witnessed the handover of IPCC complaint posters as a manifestation of the government’s continued commitment to strengthening the integrity and accountability of police personnel through strategic collaboration among various stakeholders.
The posters will be displayed at Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) information corners nationwide to raise public awareness of the IPCC’s role and the complaint channels available.
In a separate development, Saifuddin Nasution said the arrest of 12 police personnel suspected of extorting RM2 million from a Vanuatu national demonstrated the force’s zero tolerance for misconduct among its own personnel.
Yesterday, Dang Wangi police chief ACP Sazalee Adam confirmed the arrest of 12 police personnel of various ranks for allegedly extorting RM2 million from a Vanuatu national. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says creation of Malay reserve land in KL proves commitment to Bumiputera interests
Article:
TAMPIN, July 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has dismissed claims that his administration is neglecting the interests of the Bumiputera community, particularly the Malays, citing the creation of new Malay reserve land in Kuala Lumpur as proof of the government’s commitment.
Anwar said that after taking office in 2022, his administration moved to address the declining amount of Malay reserve land in the capital.
“Since Independence in 1957, no new Malay reserve land had been created in Kuala Lumpur. Existing land was simply being sold off.
“When I became Prime Minister in 2022, we reclaimed the 480-acre (194.3-hectare) Bandar Malaysia site in 2023, land previously been held by China and a private company. I reclaimed it because regulations had been violated,” he said while addressing the Semarak Kenegaraan (Patriotism) programme at Syed Sirajuddin Camp here today.
Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
Anwar said the reclaimed land was placed under the management of Petronas and Khazanah Nasional, which he described as Malay-controlled entities.
“Within the area, I designated 50 acres (20 hectares) as Malay reserve land, comprising some of the most valuable land in Kuala Lumpur,” he said.
The Prime Minister also said the proposal received no objections from DAP when it was presented to the Cabinet.
He said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke had only sought an explanation for the move.
“I explained that Malay landholdings in Kuala Lumpur were shrinking. It is my responsibility to send a clear signal. He (Loke) agreed.
“There were no objections at the Cabinet meeting. Therefore, for the first time since Independence in 1957, the Madani Government has designated some of Kuala Lumpur’s most valuable land as Malay reserve land,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Cabinet to decide Wednesday whether to release Tabung Haji RCI report
Article:
TAMPIN, July 27 — The Cabinet will decide on Wednesday whether to make public the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
He said the issue would be deliberated at the weekly Cabinet meeting before a final decision is made on the report’s release.
“There has been some debate over Tabung Haji. I do not wish to comment at length, but hopefully at Wednesday’s Cabinet meeting we can reach a decision. There is a report, and the public should be allowed to read it.
“If nothing is wrong, stand up for it. If something is wrong, prosecute. If found guilty and sentenced to prison, then serve the sentence. It has nothing to do with me. Our system is clear; investigations are carried out by the investigating authorities, prosecutions by the Attorney General, and judgments by the courts. That is not the Prime Minister’s job,” he said at the Semarak Kenegaraan programme at Syed Sirajuddin Camp here today.
Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Armed Forces Chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
Anwar said that as Prime Minister, he was duty-bound to act with integrity and adhere to the constitutional process and established legal procedures.
Last Thursday, Anwar said the government was prepared to release the final RCI report on TH soon to allow the public to learn the findings of the inquiry into allegations involving the sale of TH’s strategic assets.
The Prime Minister said he would consult the Chief Secretary to the Government on whether the report needed to be referred to the Cabinet first. — Bernama

Title: Johor exco confirms Network School has not appealed, business licence revoked and operations halted
Article:
KULAI, July 27 — The local authorities have yet to receive an appeal from the Network School for the resumption of operations following the revocation of its business licence last week.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) has yet to receive an appeal application from the Network School’s representative.
He said that the Network School is understood to have ceased its business operations.
“It (the business licence) has been cancelled and the entity is considered ‘illegal’.
“However, if they form another company and meet the set conditions, it can be considered. But there has been no appeal by them so far,” he told reporters after attending a TVET (Technical and Vocational Education and Training) event at the Kulai Municipal Career Carnival 2026 at Dewanraya Putra in Bandar Putra here today.
Mohd Jafni explained that at the municipal level, there were two obvious violations committed by the Network School.
“One was where its advertisement failed to comply with the set conditions and it has since been revoked.
“At the same time, the licence they had and their business operations are very different. Basically, they violated the licence conditions, which is why we are terminating and revoking it,” he said.
Mohd Jafni assured the public that the state government still welcomes new investments as Johor is an investor-friendly state.
He pointed out that all investors, companies and any parties investing in Johor are subject to the respective local authorities by-laws and guidelines.
Mohd Jafni said the MBIP will give the Network School’s management up to 14 days to submit an appeal.
The Bukit Permai assemblyman said MBIP will cancel its business licence after the period is up.
“Any form of action against the company owner will be under the jurisdiction of the Johor State Legal Advisor.
“At the local authority level, we are only empowered to cancel their business licence,” he explained.
Last Wednesday, it was reported that MBIP had ordered the closure of the Network School’s premises in Forest City, Iskandar Puteri.
